{"parentUuid":"40b7092c-c13e-410b-880f-c79d3a86ece2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c8a176eb-ca1e-416b-91c0-b9090afb20cb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MxXhLwsDUiYDWbDkSgiUjw","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-004-publish-auto-deploys.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"185b6fe3-9a77-4d52-a864-73f1de94d7cb","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:18:15.655Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-004-publish-auto-deploys.md","content":"# ADR-004: Publishing automatically rebuilds and deploys the public site\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-14\n\n## Context\n\nADR-001 makes the public site a static export, so a change is invisible to\nreaders until `site/` is rebuilt and pushed to GitHub Pages. The posters (coach,\ncaptain, team manager) are not technical and post mid-season; the whole point of\nthe site is that players stop asking \"when is practice?\" in the group chat. A\npractice schedule that is \"published\" but not on the website fails that goal.\n\nOptions considered: an admin-only \"Update public site\" button (editors' posts\nwait for the coach); a button any account can press (posters must remember a\nsecond step); the webmaster running `cms publish` and `cms deploy` by hand\n(readers wait hours); rebuilding and deploying automatically on every change to\npublished content.\n\n## Decision\n\nAny change to published content (publish, edit, unpublish, delete) triggers a\nsite update: rebuild `site/` and deploy it to the `gh-pages` branch. If the\ndeploy fails, the publish fails too. The content returns to its previous\nstate and the poster is told to try again later, so \"Published\" in the console\nalways means \"on the website\".\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The team laptop must hold GitHub push access (read from the environment, never\n  committed) and be online to publish.\n- No wifi means no publishing. The posters accept this in exchange for never\n  seeing a \"published but not live\" state.\n- ADR-001's consequence \"content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs\"\n  no longer describes what posters experience; the step still exists, but the\n  console runs it for them.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"40b7092c-c13e-410b-880f-c79d3a86ece2","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"fc5d3dfb-ca35-4fab-b82c-165b34c2ebb9","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3JUqnUumw5NU9fUDh7F","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"We've worked through every open question. Below are the answers to the five questions the manual says you should be able to answer before stopping. Please confirm this matches what you decided before you run `/to-spec`.\n\n**What is a post here?** A dated entry: the weekly **practice schedule** (captain), a **tournament recap** (team manager, text only), or a **qualifying result** (coach). Results are not a separate kind of post; they're protected because only the coach writes them. Slugs are generated from the title, and a number is added if one is already taken.\n\n**What is a page?** Something long-lived that is edited in place and appears in the nav: **Season Schedule** (including live-scoring links), **Travel Lineup** and **Recruiting**. Only admins can edit pages. The home page shows the Travel Lineup first, then the newest posts.\n\n**Who may do what?**\n- **Coach (admin):** everything, including all pages, all posts, deleting results, creating each season's captain and manager accounts, and deactivating graduates.\n- **Webmaster (admin):** a backup account for when the coach is locked out.\n- **Captain and team manager (editors):** create and publish posts directly; edit and delete only their own posts; no pages, no accounts.\n- A deactivated account can't log in, and its posts stay up under its name. Nobody can deactivate their own account.\n- Posting happens only on **the team laptop**. Readers use their phones, so the public site is designed for phones first.\n\n**What does publishing mean?** One click on Publish (Save draft sits next to it). Any change to published content automatically rebuilds the site and deploys it (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change isn't saved and the poster keeps the text they typed, so the console and the website always match.\n\n**Console:** one content list covering posts and pages, with one filter bar where status comes first.\n\n**Out of scope:** photos and media, posting from a phone, search, comments, forms, scheduled publishing, revision history, multi-site, and WYSIWYG editing.\n\n**Files changed:**\n- `CONTEXT.md` now holds the full glossary.\n- `docs/adr/ADR-004-publish-auto-deploys.md` is new.\n- In `notes/client-brief.md`, the delete rule now reads \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n\n**Two risks I'd keep in the spec:**\n1. The captain is a player and could post scores in a practice post; we're relying on trust there.\n2. Auto-deploy means the team laptop holds a GitHub push token and has to be online to publish.\n\nDoes this match your understanding? They may end up being outdated very quickly.\n\nException: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. find app tests templates -type f | grep -v __pycache__; cat app/*.py | head -150; cat tests/*.py | head -80","description":"Set phase, read tracker docs and app/test code"}},"wireIngestContext":{"toolu_01W5xWDTBvek9FRorL95LVGi":{"cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"a6a653e9-d4c0-4788-9683-55e616c64462","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg3JbkbNuZJqyCWEc5cE7","requestRef":"b268c236-6b13-4cbb-9dd8-f118588c7689","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-spec","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"97d39839-d7d2-4798-803b-da1d78627694","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:21:54.637Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"97d39839-d7d2-4798-803b-da1d78627694","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c0f67da2-ebc3-4660-a8fe-7dd6a7a3d072","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01W5xWDTBvek9FRorL95LVGi","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\napp/main.py\napp/__init__.py\napp/publish.py\napp/settings.py\napp/cli.py\ntests/test_usage_report.py\ntests/test_ctx_guard.py\ntests/test_t00.py\ntests/conftest.py\ntemplates/base.html\ntemplates/public/home.html\ntemplates/admin/hello.html\n\"\"\"IPHS 400 MP2 — your CMS package.\n\nT00 ships a skeleton only: one admin page, one public page, and a publish step.\nEverything else (login, roles, posts, pages, users) is yours to build, one\nticket at a time.\n\"\"\"\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","hash":"641a86b980e33c51e034d7b2f0ef441dfc6e8d2aabc7ab76a3c98f7613423e9b","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EVqZQKMsaZpdBGRc5FWYyp","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a mistake or promote the Webmaster's backup.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, delete of a published item, and deactivating an account doesn't change content so it doesn't trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"parentUuid":"f38a2e35-fdfd-466f-a2db-cba754cd5717","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3Ji3dy8FfLMtsTzUCJm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EVqZQKMsaZpdBGRc5FWYyp","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a mistake or promote the Webmaster's backup.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, delete of a published item, and deactivating an account doesn't change content so it doesn't trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":804,"cache_read_input_tokens":84483,"output_tokens":4911,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":51},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":804,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4911,"cache_read_input_tokens":84483,"cache_creation_input_tokens":804,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":804},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01EVqZQKMsaZpdBGRc5FWYyp":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. {"parentUuid":"f120f252-8d81-4831-9e98-f8df64f9449d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c0f67da2-ebc3-4660-a8fe-7dd6a7a3d072","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EVqZQKMsaZpdBGRc5FWYyp","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755/scratchpad/spec.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"41c75c91-b65d-4063-9d96-b6ced70312bf","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:24:04.620Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a mistake or promote the Webmaster's backup.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, delete of a published item, and deactivating an account doesn't change content so it doesn't trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f120f252-8d81-4831-9e98-f8df64f9449d","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"other"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"11d9e0ba-2a37-49ac-b3b4-ea82da1d601e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7bd1c86c-fd3a-4ae4-ba64-29011017f5f6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","hash":"9092f38cfa322ed3f6b854238f28c745bcc49e33ed69c07ce23b6f373db1cae2","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>mattpocock-skills:to-tickets</command-message>\n<command-name>/mattpocock-skills:to-tickets</command-name>\n"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n"}]}}
