{"parentUuid":"8900d9da-482b-4517-bfde-3b6b14121898","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3JzJ1N53C5y1UyG7Gui","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here's the proposed breakdown. Each ticket is a vertical slice that can be demoed on its own, and they map onto the seven capabilities.\n\n| # | Title | Blocked by | What it delivers |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **T01** | Coach and editors log in and out | — | Accounts (email, argon2 hash, role, active flag), signed session, CSRF on the login/logout forms, and `seed_demo.py` creating one admin and one editor. Every console URL except login redirects anyone not logged in; deactivated accounts are refused at login. *Demo: log in as the Coach and see the console; log out.* |\n| **T02** | Coach manages accounts | T01 | Admin-only screen: create an account, change its role, deactivate or reactivate it. An admin can't deactivate themselves. Editors get 403 on every account URL, including typed ones. *Demo: Coach creates the Captain's account; a deactivated Captain can't log in.* |\n| **T03** | Captain and Coach write draft posts | T01 | Create, edit and delete posts as drafts: title, auto-generated de-duplicated slug (admins may edit it), Markdown body, author, timestamps. Sanitized Markdown preview. Editors can touch only their own posts, enforced on the server. *Demo: Captain drafts \"Practice schedule\" twice → `practice-schedule-2`.* |\n| **T04** | Published posts appear on the public site | T03 | One-click Publish next to Save draft, plus unpublish. Any change to published content runs a **site update** (render `site/` only for now). Home page lists published posts newest first, with one HTML file per post. Sanitized, relative paths, drafts never written. `cms publish` uses the same site update module. *Demo: Captain publishes; it's in `site/`.* |\n| **T05** | Coach manages pages; pages build the navigation | T04 | Admin-only pages (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting); editors are refused every page action. Navigation is built from published pages. The home page shows the `travel-lineup` page first, then posts. Public CSS designed for phones first. *Demo: Coach publishes the Travel Lineup and it tops the home page.* |\n| **T06** | Console dashboard and one content list | T05 | Dashboard with counts by kind and status. One list covering posts and pages, with a single filter bar (status first, then kind and author). Editors don't see page or account controls. *Demo: filter to \"draft posts by the Captain.\"* |\n| **T07** | Publishing deploys automatically; failure blocks the change | T04 | Injectable deployer passed to `create_app()`; the default pushes to `gh-pages` using a token from the environment. A change and its deploy succeed or fail together: on failure the item keeps its previous state and the form is shown again with the poster's text and an error (ADR-004). *Demo: unplug wifi, edit the lineup, see the error, and the website is unchanged.* |\n\nT02, T03 and T07 can start as soon as their blockers close; T05 → T06 is the only long chain.\n\n**Prefactor flag for T01:** `tests/test_t00.py` expects `/admin` to return 200 with \"hello admin\" when nobody is logged in, and it says not to delete it. Once T01 adds login, that test breaks. My recommendation is that T01 redirects `/admin` to login, and the T00 test logs in first using `client_as(\"admin\")`. That changes the test's setup but not what it checks."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1656,"cache_read_input_tokens":93775,"output_tokens":1813,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":196},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1656,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1813,"cache_read_input_tokens":93775,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1656,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1656},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"4f210cf8-0aef-414b-a499-6e4f3e6083ab","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg3JzHi1AmU2o3rPUn9dA","requestRef":"39e4dc4b-aa8b-44a2-9830-a3fe0e49eab9","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-tickets","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"d5ef720b-7e3b-4a58-803d-f87b9b452181","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:27:11.125Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a2823474-9b6c-436d-9932-5d3cce050755","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

Nobody can use any console screen without logging in. A deactivated account is refused at login even with the right password. The demo seed creates one admin account and one editor account so the console can be used straight away.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Accounts have an email (unique), an argon2 password hash, a role (`admin` | `editor`) and an active flag; no plain password is ever stored or logged\n- [ ] A correct email and password logs in; a wrong password or unknown email gives the same generic error\n- [ ] A deactivated account is refused at login with the correct password\n- [ ] Logout ends the session\n- [ ] Every console URL except the login page redirects someone who isn't logged in to the login page\n- [ ] The login and logout forms carry a CSRF token; a request without a valid token is rejected\n- [ ] The demo seed creates one admin and one editor, reading their passwords from the environment, and runs clean on a fresh clone\n- [ ] The T00 admin test logs in first (via `client_as(\"admin\")`) and still checks that the console answers with \"hello admin\"; the other T00 tests are unchanged and pass\n- [ ] Tests go through HTTP with the existing `client` / `client_as` fixtures\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately)\nEOF\ncat > T02.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Coach (admin) manages accounts: creates an account for this season's Captain or Team manager, changes an account's role, and deactivates a graduated Captain (or reactivates an account). Editors can't reach account management at all, including by typing the URL, as in the WordPress field notes where Users was both hidden and denied.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An admin can create an account with email, initial password and role\n- [ ] An admin can change an account's role\n- [ ] An admin can deactivate and reactivate an account; a deactivated account can't log in\n- [ ] An admin can't deactivate their own account (the request is refused, not just hidden)\n- [ ] Accounts are never deleted; a deactivated account's posts keep its name as author\n- [ ] An editor gets 403 (or a redirect) on every account-management URL and action, including direct GET and POST requests\n- [ ] The account management link appears only for admins\n- [ ] Every account form carries a CSRF token\n- [ ] Tests cover the admin/editor permission matrix through HTTP\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T01 (#{T01})\nEOF\ncat > T03.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Captain writes a weekly practice schedule, the Team manager a tournament recap, and the Coach a qualifying result, all as draft posts. A post has a title, a Markdown body, an author and timestamps. The slug is generated from the title and made unique automatically, so the Captain never types one. Editors can only change or delete posts they wrote; the Coach can change any post. A preview shows the sanitized rendered Markdown.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Any logged-in account can create a post with a title and Markdown body, saved as a draft\n- [ ] The slug is generated from the title and made unique (`practice-schedule`, `practice-schedule-2`, …); an admin may edit it, and an edited slug must still be unique\n- [ ] Each post records its author and created/updated timestamps\n- [ ] An editor can edit and delete their own posts and is refused (403) on anyone else's, including direct requests\n- [ ] An admin can edit and delete any post\n- [ ] The editor screen has a preview of the rendered Markdown, sanitized (e.g. `<script>` is stripped)\n- [ ] Drafts never appear on the public site\n- [ ] Every post form carries a CSRF token\n- [ ] Tests use a second editor account (created through the admin's account route or a fixture) to prove \"own posts only\"\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T01 (#{T01})\nEOF\ncat > T04.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Captain publishes the practice schedule with one click, sitting next to Save draft, and it appears on the public site. An author can unpublish their own post. Any change to published content runs a **site update** that rebuilds the public site from all published content. For now a site update only renders it; deploying comes in T07. The home page lists published posts newest first, and every post gets its own page.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The editor screen has Save draft and Publish side by side; Publish takes one click\n- [ ] Authors (editors: own posts; admins: any) can unpublish a post, returning it to draft\n- [ ] Publishing, editing a published post, unpublishing, or deleting a published post runs a site update; saving or deleting a draft does not\n- [ ] The site update writes the home page (published posts, newest first, with author and date) and one HTML file per published post\n- [ ] Only published posts are written; drafts never reach the output\n- [ ] All Markdown is sanitized before it is written\n- [ ] Every `href` and `src` in the output is relative; none starts with `/`\n- [ ] `cms publish` uses the same site update module\n- [ ] Rendering tests call `render_site` into a temporary directory and inspect the files\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T03 (#{T03})\nEOF\ncat > T05.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Coach creates and edits the Season Schedule (with live-scoring links), Travel Lineup and Recruiting pages. Pages are admin-only, and editors are refused every page action. Published pages appear in the public site's navigation on every page. The home page shows the Travel Lineup first, then the newest posts, so a player sees \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\" on one screen. The public site is designed for phones first.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An admin can create, edit, publish, unpublish and delete pages, with the same fields as posts (title, unique slug, Markdown body, status, author, timestamps)\n- [ ] An editor is refused (403) on every page action, including direct requests\n- [ ] The public navigation lists every published page and no draft pages, on every public page\n- [ ] The home page shows the published page with slug `travel-lineup` first (if one exists), then published posts newest first\n- [ ] Page changes run a site update under the same rules as posts\n- [ ] Public pages are readable on a ~375px-wide phone with no horizontal scroll\n- [ ] All output paths remain relative, and Markdown remains sanitized\n- [ ] The demo seed adds the three pages (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and a few posts, at least one draft and one published\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T04 (#{T04})\nEOF\ncat > T06.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe console home becomes a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status. One content list holds both posts and pages, with a single filter bar (status first, then kind and author), fixing the WordPress problems in the field notes: the status filter was hidden away, and posts and pages lived in separate menus. Editors see only the controls they may use.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts of draft and published posts and pages\n- [ ] One content list shows posts and pages together, newest updated first\n- [ ] A single filter bar filters by status, kind and author, in that order, and the filters combine (e.g. draft posts by the Captain)\n- [ ] Each row links to its editor screen when the account may edit it\n- [ ] Editors see no page-creation or account-management controls\n- [ ] Tests check counts and filter results through HTTP\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- T05 (#{T05})\nEOF\ncat > T07.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nPublishing really puts content on the website: every site update now also deploys the public site to GitHub Pages, so \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\" (ADR-004). If the deploy fails (no wifi at the course hotel), the change isn't saved: the item keeps its previous state, and the form comes back with the poster's typed text and an error so they can retry.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `create_app()` accepts a deployer; the default pushes the rebuilt site to the `gh-pages` branch, with GitHub access read from the environment (never committed)\n- [ ] A successful publish, edit of published content, unpublish, or delete of published content renders and then deploys once\n- [ ] When the deployer fails, the change is rolled back: a new publish stays a draft;
